newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Gold closes firmer at day's high in Hong Kong.
newsitem.headline: Gold closes firmer at day's high in Hong Kong.

text.p: Gold closed firmer at the day's high on Thursday on physical demand and late overseas buying after its overnight fall in New York, dealers said.
Bullion ended at US$339.50/340.00 an ounce against New York's US$338.90/339.40 close on Wednesday and Hong Kong's previous close of US$341.40/90.

"Gold came under pressure after Belgian central bank officials said on Wednesday the Belgian government proposed increasing the amount of central bank gold that can be sold," a senior bullion dealer said.
Belgium proposed raising the amout of central bank gold that can be sold as commemorative gold coins to 26 tonnes a year from 1999 onwards, to a maximum of 133 tonnes.

"But market players were shortcovering, believing that gold had seen its lowest point and was recovering," another dealer added. "I guess the price of gold will continue steady to firm later and pick up to above US$340 levels."
Local gold ended HK$17 lower at HK$3,143 a tael.
The carry over charge at the Chinese Gold and Silver Exchange Society remained unchanged at -8.00.
